args.request: Please make a widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1 using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . I've always found this mission fascinating, and I'm a little worried about getting the two Voyager spacecraft mixed up when explaining it. What I have in mind is 9 seconds total, completely silent with no narration, music, or sound effects, split into three equal 3-second scenes showing the probe near Earth, then Jupiter, then Saturn. The scene labels should be exactly 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', and 'Saturn flyby: 1980', in that order. Please also keep the exact labels 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout, so those and the three scene labels are the five supplied labels to use. The visual style is up to you as long as the planets are recognizable and the probe matches its real dish-and-boom design, and please don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.

text:
Your Voyager 1 fact clip is done: https://videos.magichour.ai/ is not where it lives, so use this link:
http://127.0.0.1:8000/films/8f9231e69a074e7d8662c2482f2062bb.mp4

What it is:
- 9.1 seconds, widescreen (864×474), completely silent. No narration, music or sound effects.
- Three 3-second scenes in order: the probe leaving Earth, then passing Jupiter (cloud bands and Great Red Spot), then passing Saturn (rings). Uranus and Neptune do not appear.
- Every scene asks for the probe's real look: the big white high-gain dish on a ten-sided bus, with the long magnetometer boom, the science boom and the power boom.
- The labels: each scene started from a still picture made with "Voyager 1", "Source: NASA Science" and that scene's label, so the words stay on screen for the whole scene.

Please check two things, because I couldn't look at the finished frames from here:
- The spelling of all five labels. Image models usually get text right but sometimes misspell it.
- That the probe looks the same in all three scenes. Each scene was made separately, so small differences are possible.
If a label is wrong or the probe changes, tell me which scene and I'll remake just that one.

On the NASA page: I couldn't open the link with my tools, so the dates come from your labels. They match NASA's published facts: launch on September 5, 1977, Jupiter flyby in March 1979, Saturn flyby in November 1980. One way to keep the two probes apart: Voyager 2 actually launched first, on August 20, 1977. It is the only one that went on to Uranus and Neptune. Voyager 1 left the planets behind after Saturn.
